brief: Write the diagnosis encyclopedia (the in-game Codex) — pure data implementing Diagnosis (src/core/case.ts). One file per category under src/content/diagnoses/ (refractive.ts, binocular.ts, lids-conjunctiva.ts, cornea.ts, uvea-glaucoma.ts, lens.ts, retina.ts, neuro.ts, normal.ts), each `export default Diagnosis[]`. Cover EVERY canonical id in docs/GAME_DESIGN.md §8 (exactly those ids — tests/content.test.ts has the list; aim for 100% coverage). Per entry: name (proper clinical name), aka (lay/alternative names), category, summary (2-4 rich sentences: what it is, who gets it, why it matters), keyFindings (3-6 exam findings that clinch it — specific with numbers/grades/signs), typicalUrgency, pearls (2-4 high-yield exam/board pearls, discriminators vs look-alikes, red flags), rarity, reference (a real EyeWiki/StatPearls/AAO URL you verified). Use docs/research/02-clinical-cases.md and 03-test-mechanics.md and verify with WebSearch (load via ToolSearch 'select:WebSearch'). Tone: clear, elegant, memorable; player-facing so never any sin words. Validate: npx vitest run tests/content.test.ts and npm run check:mod -- src/content/diagnoses. Accuracy is the #1 criterion.

You write CLINICAL CASES (pure data) for Lumen. Contract: ClinicalCase in src/core/case.ts; findings built with buildFindings(age, sparsePatch) from @core (src/core/clinical-defaults.ts gives a healthy exam; override only what differs). Vocabulary for findings is the union types in src/core/clinical.ts — use them exactly. Diagnosis ids: ONLY the canonical list in docs/GAME_DESIGN.md §8 (tests/content.test.ts enforces it). Test ids: src/core/tests.ts. Primary clinical source: docs/research/02-clinical-cases.md and docs/research/03-test-mechanics.md (plus docs/research/00-RESEARCH-REPORT.md) — and verify anything doubtful with WebSearch (load via ToolSearch 'select:WebSearch') against EyeWiki/AAO/AOA/StatPearls.

Each case file: src/content/cases/<group>/<case-id>.ts with `export default <ClinicalCase>` (or an array). Requirements per case:
- A memorable, diverse patient (name, age, sex, occupation, one-line personality, AvatarSpec with skin 0-5, a HairStyle value, hair/iris/outfit colours, glasses if they wear them, headwear/accessory variety; ages from children to 90s; diverse backgrounds treated respectfully). The chief complaint in the patient's own voice — vivid, human, sometimes funny, never mocking.
- 6-10 history questions across categories with relevance key/helpful/neutral/red-herring; answers in the patient's voice. The key questions must be the ones a good clinician asks (onset, laterality, pain, photophobia, discharge, flashes/floaters, curtain, headache/jaw claudication, systemic disease, meds, contact lens wear, trauma...).
- Findings that are internally consistent and realistic for the diagnosis (VA logMAR + pinhole behaviour, refraction in minus-cyl, keratometry, pupils incl. RAPD, motility/deviation in prism dioptres, slit-lamp signs, van Herick, cells/flare SUN grades, fluorescein pattern, IOP, CDR & disc, vessels, lesions with zones/density, fields, Amsler, colour vision, external signs that show on the avatar: redEye, tearing, ptosis, proptosis, squinting, photophobia, templeTenderness, rash). If a sign is unilateral, put it on the correct eye only.
- essentialTests = the tests without which you cannot make the call; helpfulTests = supportive/rule-out tests. differentials: 3-5 plausible, *teachable* distractors (each must be a canonical id, not the answer).
- urgency (routine/soon/urgent/emergency) per current guidelines; management (2-4 sentences: what you do, who you refer to, how fast); 3-5 teachingPoints (crisp pearls that discriminate from the differentials); redFlags where relevant; emergency: { timeLimitSec } (90-180) ONLY for true time-critical emergencies; sources: 1-3 URLs you actually used.
- difficulty 1-5 spread across the set; tags (e.g. 'red-eye','sudden-vision-loss','paediatric','contact-lens').
- Player-facing text must never contain sin words (tests/content.test.ts checks).
Validate with: npx vitest run tests/content.test.ts  and  npm run check:mod -- src/content/cases/<group>. Both must pass for YOUR files (diagnosis entries may still be in progress by a colleague — the test tolerates a missing Diagnosis registry but not non-canonical ids). Clinical accuracy is the #1 criterion: a practising optometrist will review every number.

YOUR GROUP: src/content/cases/vision-binocular-neuro/ — write 16 cases covering: myopia (teen struggling with the board), hyperopia (child or 30s with eyestrain), astigmatism, presbyopia (classic 45-year-old 'arms too short'), anisometropia, amblyopia (child), convergence-insufficiency (student reading fatigue), accommodative-esotropia (toddler eye turning in), intermittent-exotropia, cn6-palsy (diabetic with horizontal diplopia worse at distance), cn4-palsy (vertical diplopia, head tilt), cn3-palsy WITH pupil involvement (emergency: aneurysm — timer), horner-syndrome, adie-pupil, optic-neuritis (young woman, pain on eye movement, RAPD, red desaturation), papilledema (headache, obese young woman, bilateral disc oedema — urgent), pituitary-adenoma (bitemporal hemianopia), homonymous-hemianopia (stroke), giant-cell-arteritis (elderly, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, pale swollen disc — emergency, timer), congenital-color-deficiency (male, deutan). That's 20 ideas — pick 16, prioritising teaching value, and include at least 3 emergencies with timers.

YOUR GROUP: src/content/cases/anterior/ — write 16 cases covering: dry-eye (screen worker, low TBUT, inferior/interpalpebral staining), blepharitis/meibomian dysfunction, chalazion, hordeolum, bacterial-conjunctivitis (mucopurulent, lids stuck), viral-conjunctivitis (follicles, watery, preauricular node, recent cold), allergic-conjunctivitis (itch, papillae, stringy discharge, chemosis), subconjunctival-hemorrhage (asymptomatic red patch, check BP/anticoagulants), pinguecula, pterygium, episcleritis, corneal-abrasion (linear staining, fingernail/baby), corneal-foreign-body (grinder, rust ring), hsv-keratitis (dendrite, terminal bulbs, reduced sensation), microbial-keratitis (contact lens wearer slept in lenses — urgent, round ulcer + infiltrate + AC reaction), keratoconus (young adult, scissors reflex, irregular mires, Vogt striae, Fleischer ring), herpes-zoster-ophthalmicus (dermatomal rash, Hutchinson sign), anterior-uveitis (ciliary flush, cells/flare, KPs, photophobia, small pupil, HLA-B27/back pain), acute-angle-closure (emergency with timer: halos, nausea, IOP ~50, mid-dilated fixed pupil, corneal oedema, shallow AC, van Herick 1), cataract (glare, nuclear sclerosis, myopic shift, pinhole little help), poag (asymptomatic, CDR 0.7-0.8, inferior rim thinning, arcuate defect, IOP 26), ocular-hypertension, normal-tension-glaucoma. Pick the 16 with best teaching value; include at least 2 emergencies/urgent with timers where appropriate (angle closure, microbial keratitis).

YOUR GROUP: src/content/cases/retina-emergency/ — write 14 cases covering: npdr (moderate, dot-blot + MAs + hard exudates), pdr (NVD/NVE, vitreous haemorrhage risk — urgent), diabetic-macular-edema, hypertensive-retinopathy (AV nicking, flame haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots; malignant variant with disc oedema = emergency), dry-amd (drusen, GA, slow decline), wet-amd (sudden metamorphopsia, Amsler distortion, subretinal haemorrhage — urgent), retinal-detachment (curtain, flashes/floaters, macula-on = emergency with timer), pvd (flashes/floaters, Weiss ring, no tear — still needs dilated exam same/next day), retinal-tear (horseshoe tear, Shafer sign pigment in vitreous), crao (sudden painless loss, cherry-red spot, whitening, RAPD — emergency stroke pathway, timer), crvo (blood-and-thunder, dilated tortuous veins), brvo (sectoral haemorrhages at AV crossing), central-serous (young stressed male, steroid use, blurred/dim central vision, hyperopic shift), healthy-eyes (a worried patient whose exam is completely normal — teaches restraint & reassurance; differentials should be tempting look-alikes). Include at least 3 emergencies with timers (macula-on RD, CRAO, + one more).
